01.speaker: A
01.text: I’d like us to test a single handover at four instead of asking staff to attend two short meetings. The morning team has already said it would free up time.

01.speaker: B
01.text: Can I pick up on that? The evening team starts at five. Unless we give them another route to raise problems, they’ll receive decisions without having a chance to influence them.

01.speaker: A
01.text: Fair point. What if we make the four o’clock meeting a trial and leave a written channel open until six?

01.speaker: B
01.text: That would address my main concern, provided members of the evening team can see who is responsible for each issue.

01.speaker: A
01.text: Agreed. Let’s check coverage by Friday and review unresolved cases after two weeks.

02.speaker: A
02.text: Our survey shows fifty-five per cent support for hybrid meetings. Last year it was forty per cent, so that’s a rise of fifteen percentage points.

02.speaker: B
02.text: That’s worth reporting, but the number of replies fell from one hundred to eighty. We also invited more staff this time, which means the response rate was lower.

02.speaker: A
02.text: So the headline should refer to respondents, not to the whole organisation. Do we know whether evening staff answered at the same rate?

02.speaker: B
02.text: No. The last question was optional and few people stated their shift. I’d use the result to design a pilot, but not to claim the change caused people to be more satisfied.

02.speaker: A
02.text: Agreed. Let’s collect feedback by shift during the pilot.

03.speaker: A
03.text: The customer received twelve cases, which matches the quantity on the invoice. However, the labels on three cases showed a different batch number.

03.speaker: B
03.text: According to our dispatch log, all twelve cases had been scanned before loading. Does that tell us what was inside them?

03.speaker: A
03.text: No. It shows which labels were scanned. The labels might have been printed twice, or cases might have been exchanged after the scan.

03.speaker: B
03.text: The customer also says the seals were intact. That makes repacking during delivery less likely, but it doesn’t rule out a mistake at the warehouse.

03.speaker: A
03.text: Let’s keep the three cases aside, check the print history and request the driver’s record by tomorrow.

04.speaker: A
04.text: The three-month package comes to nine hundred pounds. That includes support, but there’s a separate installation charge of one hundred and twenty.

04.speaker: B
04.text: Our budget is a thousand pounds. Could you waive half the installation charge if we pay the first month upfront?

04.speaker: A
04.text: We could reduce the charge to sixty pounds, provided that your first payment clears before installation. I’d need my manager’s approval to promise Friday support.

04.speaker: B
04.text: Then we can agree the price in principle. However, we can’t confirm the package until Friday support is included in writing.

04.speaker: A
04.text: Understood. I’ll ask my manager and send a revised offer by noon tomorrow.

05.speaker: A
05.text: My essay says the city should replace some parking with bike lanes. I wrote about safety and the effect on shops, but I can’t find a third point.

05.speaker: B
05.text: How about how the lanes connect to public transport? That would be different from safety and would explain who might use them.

05.speaker: A
05.text: Good idea. I’ve also said all businesses will benefit. That sounds stronger than the report.

05.speaker: B
05.text: You could say some businesses might benefit from more local visits, whereas deliveries might be harder if loading bays disappear.

05.speaker: A
05.text: I’ll recommend a trial on two streets and keep loading access as a condition. That gives the conclusion a clear decision.

06.speaker: A
06.text: The headline says the free workshop was a complete success. You helped organise it. Would you agree with that?

06.speaker: B
06.text: To be fair, every weekday place was booked. But if by success you mean it reached everyone who needed it, I wouldn’t go that far.

06.speaker: A
06.text: Are you saying the figures were wrong?

06.speaker: B
06.text: No, the booking figures are accurate. They just don’t include people who had to work during those hours or people who tried to book after all the places had gone.

06.speaker: A
06.text: So you’d report that demand was strong at the times offered, and then test another time before making a wider claim?

06.speaker: B
06.text: Exactly. A weekend session would give us a better comparison.

07.speaker: A
07.text: I chose make in the phrase make a deadline. It sounded natural because I say make a decision all the time.

07.speaker: B
07.text: With a deadline, meet means finish on time. Look at the whole phrase, not just whether a verb is grammatical.

07.speaker: A
07.text: I also wrote available in the gap after the. The sentence says the room could not be booked.

07.speaker: B
07.text: Then the gap needs a noun and a negative meaning: the unavailability of the room.

07.speaker: A
07.text: For the transformation, I’ll count the words including the key word and check whether I’ve kept the original time reference.

08.speaker: A
08.text: In both pictures people are learning a new skill. The workshop looks more hands-on, whereas the online class seems easier to fit around work.

08.speaker: B
08.text: Which setting would help someone build confidence more quickly?

08.speaker: A
08.text: The workshop might, because you can notice mistakes while you’re doing the task. On the other hand, someone who lives far away may be more likely to attend online regularly.

08.speaker: B
08.text: So are you suggesting that access matters more than immediate feedback?

08.speaker: A
08.text: It depends on the learner. Beginners may need direct support, but people with some experience might benefit from a flexible online option.

09.speaker: A
09.text: Ana has just moved here and wants to join the evening course. She can’t use stairs, and she’s not sure which document to bring.

09.speaker: B
09.text: The Spanish notice says the main entrance has steps. The side entrance is accessible, but she has to request access when she registers.

09.speaker: A
09.text: Could she get one of the free places if she has only just moved?

09.speaker: B
09.text: She can apply if she can provide proof of address. But the notice says places are limited, so she should wait for a confirmation before making plans.

09.speaker: A
09.text: I’ll send her a short message with the key steps and offer to help if she isn’t sure about the document.

10.speaker: A
10.text: The venue’s first email offered us Room Green at one hundred and twenty pounds. The latest message says the lift will be out of service on Friday.

10.speaker: B
10.text: Does that change the start time? We have twenty-six participants and two need step-free access.

10.speaker: A
10.text: The time is unchanged. Room Blue is available downstairs and costs one hundred and ten, but it holds twenty. Two smaller sessions would cost one hundred and forty.

10.speaker: B
10.text: That’s within the one hundred and fifty pound limit, but we’ll need to confirm whether everyone can attend the new times.

10.speaker: A
10.text: Exactly. I’ll ask the venue to hold both slots until tomorrow at noon and write to the group today.
